questions.question: In the simulator, which trace is a shortcut rather than a sound rationale?
options: It gets the answer right but sets rationale_sound to False
It gets the answer wrong and has a sound rationale
It is always sampled on OOD tasks
It is discarded before answer accuracy is measured
questions.explanation: A shortcut trace can be correct, but the model marks its rationale as unsound; the ID/OOD difference changes its answer probability, not that label.

questions.question: For a model with probabilities sound=.20, shortcut=.40, random=.40, what does evaluate measure separately?
options: Only the fraction of sound traces
Answer accuracy and the fraction of evaluated traces whose rationale is sound
Only whether shortcut traces work OOD
The number of generated traces, without their answers
questions.explanation: evaluate counts correct answers for accuracy and counts rationale_sound for rationale soundness, so a correct shortcut affects the two metrics differently.

questions.question: In one idealized STaR update, why can sound=.20, shortcut=.40, random=.40 move toward approximately .38, .40, .22?
options: The update deletes every shortcut trace
The alpha value replaces the old model with a uniform distribution
Correct traces are filtered, their sound/shortcut/random shares are measured, and alpha=.6 blends those shares with the old probabilities
The OOD accuracy of shortcuts is copied into the sound probability
questions.explanation: The expected kept shares are .50, .40, and .10; with alpha .6, blending them with the old vector gives .38, .40, and .22.

questions.question: What is the main effect of V-STaR's score when it compares traces?
options: It selects the shortest rationale regardless of correctness
It gives every wrong trace the same score as a sound trace
It evaluates only the first sampled trace
It makes a sound correct trace score higher than a shortcut or wrong trace
questions.explanation: The score is .9 for a sound trace, .55 for a correct shortcut, and .3 for a wrong trace, so sampling can favor a sound explanation.

questions.question: Why can STaR reinforce a shortcut on an OOD task?
options: It retains traces because they are correct, even though a shortcut is correct only .05 of the time OOD and has no sound rationale
It forces every OOD answer to use the sound branch
It scores every incorrect trace above a correct sound trace
It changes the OOD shortcut probability to .40 before filtering
questions.explanation: STaR's filter sees correctness, not causal validity. A shortcut that happens to be correct can therefore enter the training set without a sound rationale.

questions.question: What does increasing V-STaR from one sample to 16 samples change?
options: It guarantees every selected trace is sound
It gives more chances to find a high-scoring sound trace, but does not make the guarantee absolute
It removes the OOD penalty from shortcuts
It prevents the model from generating random traces
questions.explanation: More samples increase the chance that at least one sound, correct trace is available for selection; the simulator still samples stochastically.
